relevance_note: Exome cohort paper in which three families carry a homozygous GAMT variant; two treated CCDS2 patients get individual-level features: "These two patients both showed improvement of aggressive behavior and autistic features".
method_note: Hand-built JSON via a short script in scratch. The GAMT families AQ39, AQ40 and TR28 (7 affected: Table 1 '2/5; 2/6; 3/4', Table S1 '7/15') are described only at family/group level (one merged Table 1 row), so they get no individual rows; n_patients_reported=7. Only the two patients whose treatment response was monitored get rows (rule 6 labels 'unnamed person 1/2'), because the text gives them features; it is not stated which family each belongs to, so family_label is not reported. Their features come from one statement about 'these two patients both', recorded as observed with evidence_basis 'inferred from group statement'. The Table 1 family-row phenotype 'Intellectual disability, movement disorder with myoclonic jerks' was NOT attributed to the two individuals (row covers three families; not stated per person). Variant, zygosity (hom) and 'pathogenic' come from the single Table 1 GAMT row naming the three families, which these CCDS2 patients belong to. Genomic coordinates are from Table S1 columns Chr/Start/End/Ref/Alt; no genome build printed. Inheritance: 'AR' is the mode, not an origin, so not reported; segregation testing is described only for the cohort in general. cohort_size_as_stated null: the paper gives 83 families and 102 exomes, not a patient total. cites_prior_report false: the GAMT row carries no asterisk (the asterisked previously published families are all other genes); reference [42] cites the variant, not the patients. Treatment: the paper says specific treatment was enabled and response monitored, and names creatine supplementation only as part of recommendations/previous reports, so the regimen is not asserted. No contradictions found.
